hypothesis: The integration of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques with de novo molecular design can significantly enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of drug discovery processes. By leveraging RAG to access and synthesize relevant chemical knowledge and data, researchers can better navigate the vast chemical space and generate novel drug-like candidates that meet complex biological constraints, thereby reducing the time and cost associated with traditional drug design methods [self-rag:29][denovo-genai-survey:1][27][28][29][30]. This approach not only facilitates the exploration of unknown chemical spaces but also improves the accuracy of predictions in molecular and protein generation tasks, ultimately accelerating the development of innovative therapeutics [denovo-genai-survey:1][34][35].
